newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Retail sales rose a strong 1.5 percent in January, Commerce Department data showed, raising jitters the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates soon and sending stocks sharply lower.
* U.S. shares registered their biggest drop since last July as rising interest rates created concern about the market's valuation.
* Ford Motor's chairman and chief executive officer Alexander Trotman would stay on until 2000, 18 months past the company's normal retirement age of 65.
* Consolidated Edison and New York state regulators agreed on a pact to restructure the utility, cutting rates for large industrial customers and splitting it up into units.

* Conrail chairman David LeVan would get a $22 million golden parachute if Federal regulators approve a plan to divide the railroad company between CSX and Norfolk Southern, a source close to the deal said.
* The White House and Republicans in Congress face another potential deadlock in the latest attempts to balance the budget.
* A 39-year-old University of Chicago professor is set to win the John Bates Clark Medal from the American Economic Association, economists on the awards panel said.
* Japan's gross domestic product grew one percent in the fourth quarter compared with the prior three months, helped by exports.

* The American Stock Exchange voted to quote share prices in trading increments of 1/16 of a dollar compared with the eighths of a dollar now used. Two Congressmen introduced legislation aimed at making exchanges switch to a decimal-based quotation system.
* Barnes & Noble posted better-than-expected fourth quarter profits, helped by sales at older superstores. But the company said it planned to slow expansion.
* Conservative Republican Senator Orrin Hatch and Senator Edward Kennedy, a Democrat, joined to back a bill providing health insurance to the nation's uninsured children.
* The big three denim jean makers -- Levi Strauss, Guess Inc and VF Corp -- face a tough battle for market share against new, fashion-conscious competition.
* Delta makes a surprise choice to hire Cordiant Plc's Saatchi & Saatchi as a new advertising agency.
